title: Primary Headaches: Migraine, Tension-Type, and Cluster Headache

steps.tx: A common neurovascular disorder characterised by recurrent episodes of unilateral, pulsating, moderate-to-severe headache accompanied by nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia is migraine. In up to thirty percent of patients, the headache phase is preceded or accompanied by transient, fully reversible focal neurological symptoms, designated as **migraine with aura**.
steps.say: A common neurovascular disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of unilateral, pulsating headache with nausea and light sensitivity is migraine. In thirty percent of patients, the headache phase is preceded by transient focal neurological symptoms, designated as migraine with aura.

steps.tx: The underlying neurophysiological substrate responsible for the migraine aura is a wave of neuronal and glial depolarisation slowly propagating across the cerebral cortex, termed **cortical spreading depression**. This depolarising wavefront moves across the occipital cortex at two to six millimetres per minute, followed by prolonged cortical oligemia, producing classic scintillating scotomas and expanding visual fortification spectra.
steps.say: The underlying neurophysiological substrate responsible for the migraine aura is a wave of cellular depolarisation slowly propagating across the cerebral cortex, termed cortical spreading depression. Moving at three millimetres per minute, it produces classic scintillating scotomas and visual fortification spectra.

steps.tx: Acute abortive therapy for moderate to severe acute migraine attacks relies on selective serotonin 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonists, collectively designated as **triptans** (such as sumatriptan, zolmitriptan, or rizatriptan). Triptans induce intracranial arterial vasoconstriction, inhibit peripheral trigeminal calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) release, and block central trigeminal nociceptive transmission, though they are strictly contraindicated in coronary artery disease.
steps.say: Acute abortive therapy for moderate to severe migraine attacks relies on selective 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonists, designated as triptans. Triptans induce cranial vasoconstriction and block calcitonin gene-related peptide release, though they are contraindicated in established coronary artery disease.

rows: First-line acute abortive therapy for moderate to severe attacks
Acute abortive therapy for mild to moderate attacks
Acute abortive therapy when triptans are contraindicated

steps.tx: When migraine headaches occur four or more days per month, cause severe functional disability, or fail acute therapies, pharmacological **migraine prophylaxis** is indicated. Evidence-based first-line preventive options include beta-blockers (propranolol), calcium channel blockers (flunarizine), tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline), and anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies (erenumab, galcanezumab).
steps.say: When migraine headaches occur four or more days monthly, cause functional disability, or fail acute therapies, pharmacological migraine prophylaxis is indicated. First-line preventive options include beta-blockers, flunarizine, amitriptyline, and anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies.

points: Limit to < 10 days/month to avoid MOH

steps.tx: An effective first-line prophylactic antiepileptic agent proven to reduce monthly migraine frequency is **topiramate**. Through multiple mechanisms, including voltage-gated sodium channel blockade, GABA-A receptor potentiation, AMPA/kainate glutamate inhibition, and carbonic anhydrase inhibition, topiramate suppresses cortical hyperexcitability, though patients must be counselled regarding paraesthesias, cognitive slowing, weight loss, and teratogenicity.

Through sodium channel blockade, GABA potentiation, and carbonic anhydrase inhibition, topiramate dampens cortical hyperexcitability, though patients must be monitored for cognitive slowing and weight loss.

rows: Paresthesias, cognitive slowing, kidney stones, weight loss

steps.tx: The most prevalent primary headache disorder worldwide is the non-pulsatile, dull, bilateral band-like ache classified as **tension-type headache**. Lacking nausea, vomiting, or focal neurological aura, the headache is characterised by mild-to-moderate constricting tightness across the forehead or occiput, frequently provoked by musculoskeletal pericranial muscle myofascial tenderness and emotional stress.
steps.say: The most prevalent primary headache disorder worldwide is the non-pulsatile, dull, bilateral band-like ache classified as tension-type headache. Lacking nausea, vomiting, or neurological aura, it is characterized by mild to moderate constricting tightness provoked by pericranial muscle tenderness and emotional stress.

left.title: Tension-Type Headache
points: Mild to moderate intensity; not aggravated by walking
Absence of nausea, vomiting, or photophobia

right.title: Migraine Headache
points: Moderate to severe; aggravated by physical exertion

steps.tx: A severe trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia characterised by excruciating, strictly unilateral, periorbital or retro-orbital stabbing pain is **cluster headache**. Occurring predominantly in young male smokers, attacks last fifteen to one-hundred-eighty minutes and recur at identical times daily (peaking during REM sleep), accompanied by ipsilateral cranial autonomic features including lacrimation, conjunctival injection, nasal congestion, and partial Horner syndrome.
steps.say: A severe trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia characterized by excruciating unilateral periorbital stabbing pain is cluster headache. Occurring predominantly in young male smokers, attacks last up to three hours and recur at identical times daily, accompanied by ipsilateral eye redness, tearing, and nasal congestion.

vis.alt: Clinical features and ipsilateral autonomic signs in acute cluster headache.
vis.caption: Periorbital agonizing pain and parasympathetic autonomic activation in cluster headache. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The acute first-line treatment of choice for aborting an acute cluster headache attack is inhalation of one-hundred percent **high-flow oxygen** delivered via a non-rebreather face mask at ten to fifteen litres per minute for fifteen minutes, or subcutaneous sumatriptan (6 mg). Transition and long-term prophylactic prevention require verapamil titrated with electrocardiographic monitoring of the PR interval.
steps.say: The acute first-line treatment of choice for aborting a cluster headache attack is inhalation of one-hundred percent high-flow oxygen via a non-rebreather mask at twelve litres per minute, or subcutaneous sumatriptan. Long-term prophylaxis requires verapamil titrated with electrocardiographic monitoring.

rows: Rapid relief within 15 min; safe for multiple daily uses
Fastest pharmacological relief; limit to 2 doses/day
Rapid bridging while verapamil titration takes effect
First-line preventative; requires serial ECGs for PR block
